ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Low-Rank Channel Mixing on a Channel-Independent Encoder
PROPOSAL: Attach a low-rank cross-variate mixing layer of rank eight to a channel-independent patch encoder, so that each variate receives a learned combination of summary tokens from the others at a cost linear in channel count. Train with mean squared error on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather, and Electricity with lookback 96 and horizons 96, 192, 336, and 720, using three seeds. Report test error and training time against the plain channel-independent encoder, and track the learned mixing matrix for structure.
CONTROLS: Compare with PatchTST, iTransformer, and DLinear under identical splits and normalisation. Ablate the mixing by freezing it at random values and by replacing it with a fixed average over variates.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Error should drop by about 3 percent on Weather and Electricity relative to the channel-independent encoder, at under 1.2 times its training time. It may fail on the ETT sets, where variates are few and nearly duplicated in what they offer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Variate Attention at Four Encoder Depths
PROPOSAL: Insert full cross-variate attention into a channel-independent patch encoder at each of four depths in turn, with a variate embedding of width 64, and compare placement after the first, second, third, and fourth block. Train with mean squared error on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather, and Electricity with lookback 96 and horizons 96, 192, 336, and 720, using three seeds. Report test error and training time against the plain channel-independent encoder, and track the attention maps for structure.
CONTROLS: Compare with PatchTST, iTransformer, and DLinear under identical splits and normalisation. Ablate the attention by freezing it at random values and by replacing it with a fixed average over variates, and by shuffling the variate order.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Error should drop by about 3 percent on Weather and Electricity relative to the channel-independent encoder, whatever the placement. It may fail on the ETT sets, where variates are few and the attention adds parameters without information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Horizon-Query Cross-Attention Decoder Replacing Linear Projection
PROPOSAL: Replace the linear projection that maps encoder outputs to future values with a two-layer decoder in which learned horizon queries cross-attend to the encoded patches. Train end to end with mean squared error on ETTh1, Weather, Electricity, and Traffic with lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds, and on a lookback of 336 for the strongest setting. Report error, parameter count, and inference time, and break error down by forecast step to locate where the decoder helps.
CONTROLS: Compare with the linear head on the same encoder, an MLP head with matched parameters, and an autoregressive patch decoder. Ablate the queries by making them constant across steps, and the encoder by freezing it.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: The decoder should cut error at far horizons by about 4 percent on Electricity and Traffic while costing under 10 percent more at inference. It may fail on short horizons, where the linear head already captures the next few steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Iterative Refinement Decoder Over Encoded Patch Sequences
PROPOSAL: Swap the linear projection that maps encoder outputs to future values for a refinement decoder that starts from a draft forecast and repairs it through six passes, each reading the encoded patches and the previous draft. Train end to end with mean squared error on ETTh1, Weather, Electricity, and Traffic at lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720 with three seeds, and at lookback 336 for the strongest setting. Report error and inference time, chart error against pass index, and read the draft-to-final correction by forecast step.
CONTROLS: Compare with the linear head on the same encoder and an MLP head of matched size. Ablate weight sharing between passes, and the encoder by freezing it for the whole run.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: The decoder should cut error at far horizons by about 4 percent on Electricity and Traffic while costing under 40 percent more at inference. It may fail on short horizons, where the draft already captures the next few steps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Single-Stage Joint Reconstruction and Forecasting Objective
PROPOSAL: Train a patch encoder and a linear decoder in one stage with a loss that adds masked-patch reconstruction on the lookback window to forecasting error on the horizon, sharing the same decoder for both targets. Run on ETTh1, ETTm2, and Weather with lookback 336 and horizon 192, using five seeds. Compare against the usual pipeline that pretrains by reconstruction and then fine-tunes on forecasting, matching total gradient steps for the two. Report error, steps to reach the best validation score, and the loss-weight setting chosen on validation.
CONTROLS: Compare with supervised-only training, the two-stage pipeline, and a model pretrained on a different dataset. Ablate the reconstruction term by setting its weight to zero, and the mask ratio at 0.25 versus 0.5.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The single-stage loss should match the two-stage error within 1 percent while reaching the best score in about half the steps. It may fail on ETTm2, where the series is smooth and reconstruction offers little beyond forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pooled-Corpus Pretraining Followed by Joint Reconstruction Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a patch encoder by masked-patch reconstruction on a corpus pooling eleven public datasets, then fine-tune the encoder and a linear decoder in one stage with a loss that adds reconstruction on the lookback window to forecasting error on the horizon. Run on ETTh1, ETTm2, and Weather with lookback 336 and horizon 192, using five seeds. Compare against fine-tuning from scratch and against the usual pipeline that fine-tunes after reconstruction only. Report error, steps to reach the best validation score, and the loss-weight setting chosen on validation.
CONTROLS: Compare with supervised-only training, the two-stage pipeline, and a model pretrained on a different dataset. Ablate the reconstruction term by setting its weight to zero, and the mask ratio at 0.25 versus 0.5.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The pooled pretraining should lower error by about 2 percent over scratch training. It may fail on ETTm2, where the series is smooth and pretraining on other domains transfers little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Graph Over Learned Variate Embeddings for Sparse Cross-Channel Links
PROPOSAL: Learn an embedding for each variate of Traffic, which has 862 sensors, and build a sparse neighbour graph that links each sensor to its eight nearest embeddings, refreshed each epoch. Apply attention only along graph edges after a channel-independent patch encoder, so the cross-variate cost grows linearly with sensors. Train with mean squared error at lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds, and measure memory, training time, and error. Plot the learned graph against the known road network to see whether it recovers adjacency.
CONTROLS: Compare with dense cross-variate attention, a channel-independent encoder, and a random neighbour graph of equal degree. Ablate the neighbour count between four and sixteen, and the refresh schedule.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The sparse graph should match dense attention error within 1 percent at about a quarter of its memory. It may fail where traffic dynamics depend on distant sensors that the embedding does not place close together.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense Versus Sparse Cross-Channel Attention on Three Wide Datasets
PROPOSAL: Learn an embedding for each variate of Traffic, with 862 sensors, Electricity, with 321 clients, and Solar, with 137 plants, and build neighbour graphs of degree four, eight, sixteen, and thirty-two, refreshed each epoch. Apply attention along the graph edges after a channel-independent patch encoder, and train with mean squared error at three lookbacks and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds. Measure memory, training time, and error for each degree, lookback, and dataset. Plot the learned Traffic graph against the known road network to see whether it recovers adjacency.
CONTROLS: Compare with dense cross-variate attention, a channel-independent encoder, and a random neighbour graph of equal degree. Ablate the refresh schedule, and the embedding width.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The sparse graphs should match dense attention error within 1 percent at about a quarter of its memory. It may fail where dynamics depend on distant sensors that the embedding does not place close together.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frequency-Domain Decoder for Smooth Long-Horizon Forecasts
PROPOSAL: Replace the linear projection with a decoder that predicts the first thirty-two Fourier coefficients of the horizon from the encoded patches and inverts them to a forecast, with a small time-domain correction layer. Train with mean squared error on ETTh2, Weather, Electricity, and Solar with lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds. Report error per horizon and the energy of the residual spectrum. Check whether the gain concentrates on series with strong daily cycles.
CONTROLS: Compare with the linear head, a seasonal-trend decomposition head, and an MLP head with matched parameters. Ablate the number of coefficients and the correction layer.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Error should fall by about 3 percent on Electricity and Solar at horizon 720. It may fail on Weather, where irregular fronts leave energy in high frequencies that the truncated spectrum drops.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Wavelet-Packet Decoder With Level and Basis Search
PROPOSAL: Swap the linear projection for a decoder that predicts wavelet-packet coefficients of the horizon from the encoded patches and inverts them to a forecast, searching over four mother wavelets and five decomposition levels with a small time-domain correction layer. Train with mean squared error on ETTh2, Weather, Electricity, and Solar at lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds for each setting. Report error per horizon and the energy of the residual spectrum, and see whether the gain concentrates on series with strong daily cycles.
CONTROLS: Compare with the linear head and a trend-seasonal head of matched size. Ablate the correction layer, and the wavelet choice by fixing it to the first.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Error should fall by about 3 percent on Electricity and Solar at horizon 720, with little dependence on the wavelet. It may fail on Weather, where irregular fronts spread energy across levels that the decoder cannot separate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Factorial Study of Encoder, Decoder, and Training Choices
PROPOSAL: Cross two encoders, channel-independent and channel-dependent, with two decoders, linear and cross-attention, and two training regimes, two-stage reconstruction then forecasting and single-stage joint loss, giving eight models of matched parameter count. Train each on ETTh1, Weather, Electricity, and Traffic at lookback 96 and horizons 96 and 336, using five seeds. Fit a mixed-effects model of test error on the three factors and their interactions, with dataset as a random effect, and report which interactions survive correction for multiple tests.
CONTROLS: Compare with published numbers for PatchTST, iTransformer, and TimesNet re-run under the same splits. Ablate parameter matching by letting the decoder grow in the cross-attention cells.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The training regime should interact with the decoder, with the joint loss helping the attention decoder by about 3 percent. It may fail to show any encoder effect, since earlier reports find channel-dependent encoders gain little over independent ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Grid of Lookback, Patch Length, and Architecture Combinations
PROPOSAL: Cross two encoders, channel-independent and channel-dependent, with two decoders, linear and cross-attention, six lookback lengths from 48 to 720, and four patch lengths, giving ninety-six models of matched parameter count. Train each on ETTh1, Weather, Electricity, and Traffic at horizons 96 and 336, using five seeds. Fit a mixed-effects model of test error on the four factors and their interactions, with dataset as a random effect, and report which interactions survive correction for multiple tests.
CONTROLS: Rerun three published forecasters on the same splits for reference. Hold parameter count fixed in each cell by shrinking the encoder width where the decoder grows.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The lookback should interact with the encoder type, with channel-dependence helping at short lookbacks by about 3 percent. It may fail to show any patch-length effect, since earlier reports find it matters little once the lookback is fixed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Pretraining on a Multi-Dataset Corpus With a Shared Decoder
PROPOSAL: Train a patch encoder with a cross-attention decoder in a single stage on the pooled training splits of twelve public datasets, mixing reconstruction and forecasting losses with a weight scheduled from reconstruction-heavy to forecasting-heavy. Evaluate zero-shot and after short fine-tuning on ETTh1, ETTm2, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and Solar with horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds. Report error against dataset-specific models, and track how error moves with the share of each source dataset in the mixture.
CONTROLS: Compare with dataset-specific training, a two-stage pretrain-then-finetune encoder, and a published foundation forecaster evaluated zero-shot. Ablate the mixture by dropping one source family at a time.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The joint model should be within 3 percent of dataset-specific error after short fine-tuning. It may fail zero-shot on Solar, whose zero-heavy nights have no close analogue in the other datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dataset-Specific Joint Training Over Mixture Weights
PROPOSAL: Train a patch encoder with a cross-attention decoder in a single stage on each of six public datasets, ETTh1, ETTm2, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and Solar, mixing reconstruction and forecasting losses with a weight stepped from zero to one in tenths and scheduled from reconstruction-heavy to forecasting-heavy. Evaluate at horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds for each weight. Report error against dataset-specific supervised models, and track how error moves with the weight on each dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare with supervised-only training, a two-stage pretrain-then-finetune encoder, and a published foundation forecaster evaluated zero-shot. Ablate the schedule by fixing the weight at its start and end values.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The joint model should land within 3 percent of the best weight on each dataset with a broad optimum. It may fail on Solar, whose zero-heavy nights make the reconstruction term dominate early training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Channel Clustering to Share Decoders in Wide Datasets
PROPOSAL: Cluster the variates of Electricity by the spectrum of their training series into eight groups, and give each group its own linear decoder on top of a shared channel-independent patch encoder. Train with mean squared error at lookback 96 and horizons 96 and 336, using three seeds. Report error against a single shared decoder and against one decoder per variate, along with parameter counts. Check whether cluster membership agrees with the clients' known consumption types.
CONTROLS: Compare with a random assignment of variates to groups and with a single shared decoder. Ablate the group count among four, eight, and sixteen.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Clustered decoders should cut error by about 2 percent against one shared decoder and match per-variate decoders with far fewer parameters. It may fail where clients change type over the year, so that spectra measured on training data are a poor guide.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Variate Decoder Bags With Spectral Initialisation
PROPOSAL: Give each of the 321 variates of Electricity its own linear decoder on top of a shared channel-independent patch encoder, initialise each decoder from the spectrum of its training series, and train a bag of five decoders per variate. Train with mean squared error at lookback 96 and horizons 96 and 336, using three seeds. Report error against a single shared decoder, along with parameter counts, and see whether the decoders that drift furthest from initialisation belong to clients of a known consumption type.
CONTROLS: Compare with a random initialisation and a single shared decoder. Ablate the bag size among one, three, and five.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Per-variate decoders should cut error by about 2 percent against one shared decoder, with the bag adding little. It may fail where clients change type over the year, so that spectra measured on training data are a poor guide.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lookback Sensitivity of Cross-Channel Gains
PROPOSAL: Measure how the gain of a cross-variate encoder over a channel-independent one changes with lookback length, using a matched pair of encoders on Weather, Electricity, and ETTh1 at five lookbacks from short to long and horizon 192, with three seeds. Fit the gain as a function of lookback and the number of variates, and report where the curves cross zero. Test whether longer lookbacks let the independent encoder recover the benefit by learning the dependencies in time.
CONTROLS: Compare with a linear model of equal lookback and a patch encoder with randomly permuted variates. Ablate the cross-variate layer by sharing its weights across depth.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The gain should shrink from about 4 percent at the shortest lookback to under 1 percent at the longest. It may fail on ETTh1, where the variates are so few that the gain is noise at any lookback.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Channel Gains Under Noise, Missingness, and Dropout
PROPOSAL: Measure how the gain of a cross-variate encoder over a channel-independent one changes under three input corruptions, Gaussian noise, random missing blocks, and variate dropout, each at four strengths, using a matched pair of encoders on Weather, Electricity, and ETTh1 at two lookbacks and horizon 192, with three seeds. Regress the gain on corruption strength and variate count, and note where the fitted lines reach zero. Examine whether corrupted inputs let the independent encoder win back the benefit by learning dependencies through time.
CONTROLS: Compare with a linear model of equal lookback and a patch encoder with randomly permuted variates. Ablate the cross-variate layer by sharing its weights across depth, and by freezing it.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: The gain should grow from about 2 percent on clean inputs to 5 percent under heavy missingness. It may fail on ETTh1, where the variates are so few that the gain is noise at any strength.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: State-Space Encoder With Alternating Variate and Time Scans
PROPOSAL: Build a channel-dependent encoder from a state-space block that scans over variates and over time in alternating passes, and attach the cross-attention decoder, trained in one stage with the joint reconstruction and forecasting loss. Run on Traffic, Electricity, Weather, and Solar at lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds. Report error, memory, and throughput against a transformer with variate attention, and break the error down by horizon.
CONTROLS: Compare with PatchTST, iTransformer, and a channel-independent state-space encoder under identical splits. Ablate the variate scan by dropping it, and the joint loss by training on forecasting error alone.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The alternating scans should match variate attention error within 1 percent at roughly half its memory on Traffic. It may fail on Weather, where few variates leave the variate scan little to model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Patch Length and Stride Study of a Cross-Attention Decoder
PROPOSAL: Train a patch encoder with a cross-attention decoder under eight patch lengths and five strides, in one stage with the joint reconstruction and forecasting loss. Run on Traffic, Electricity, Weather, and Solar at lookback 96 and horizons 96 to 720, using three seeds for each pairing. Report error as a function of patch length and stride, fit a response surface, and break the error down by horizon.
CONTROLS: Compare with PatchTST with its default patching, a linear head on the same encoder, and a fixed patch length of sixteen. Ablate the joint loss by training on forecasting error alone.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Error should vary by under 2 percent across the patch settings, with a shallow optimum near sixteen. It may fail on Weather, where short patches fit irregular fronts better and the surface tilts.
